headline: Cloudflare launches new AI traffic options for website owners
summary: Cloudflare now offers granular control over AI bot traffic, allowing website owners to manage crawlers based on their purpose: Search, Agent, or Training. This provides more nuanced content protection and discoverability options.
details: A year ago, Cloudflare introduced a "Block AI Bots" option and Pay-Per-Crawl marketplace, responding to AI models using website content without compensation. This was a direct response to an "existential threat" to content owners.

However, the landscape has evolved, and a simple block-all solution is no longer sufficient. Website owners need more nuanced control to protect content while maintaining discoverability, especially for smaller sites.
Cloudflare is now moving beyond a simple "AI" definition, focusing on bot behavior and purpose. They aim to answer what bots are doing, what they're storing, and how they'll reshare content.
To address this, Cloudflare is launching the ability for customers to manage AI traffic based on three major use cases: Search, Agent, and Training crawlers. This allows for more precise control.
Bot operators are encouraged to separate their crawlers by purpose to increase transparency for website owners. This helps sites understand why a crawler is visiting and manage access accordingly.

This new classification system is designed to be scalable and representative of evolving automated traffic. It recognizes that bots can have multiple purposes and should be tracked for all of them, not just one.
caption:
Cloudflare just rolled out new tools for website owners to control AI bot traffic. Now you can manage crawlers based on their specific purpose: Search, Agent, or Training.

A year ago, Cloudflare introduced a "Block AI Bots" option and Pay-Per-Crawl marketplace, responding to AI models using website content without compensation. This was a direct response to an "existential threat" to content owners.

However, the landscape has evolved, and a simple block-all solution is no longer sufficient. Website owners need more nuanced control to protect content while maintaining discoverability, especially for smaller sites.

Cloudflare is now moving beyond a simple "AI" definition, focusing on bot behavior and purpose. They aim to answer what bots are doing, what they're storing, and how they'll reshare content.

To address this, Cloudflare is launching the ability for customers to manage AI traffic based on three major use cases: Search, Agent, and Training crawlers. This allows for more precise control.

Bot operators are encouraged to separate their crawlers by purpose to increase transparency for website owners. This helps sites understand why a crawler is visiting and manage access accordingly.

This new classification system is designed to be scalable and representative of evolving automated traffic. It recognizes that bots can have multiple purposes and should be tracked for all of them, not just one.
